data.exact_reserve_text: During 2015 the Syndicate released GBP 95.7m of technical reserves in respect of prior periods (2014: GBP 77.4m), arising predominantly from the Energy, Casualty and Treaty Divisions. These releases were due to favourable claims development on attritional losses during 2015.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Losses from this event are below GBP 10m and there has been little change in the estimated net loss for each event during 2015.

prior_year_events.event_name: Hailstorm and tornado events in the US (May and June)
prior_year_events.impact_description: A number of hailstorm and tornado events in the US in May and June. Losses from each of these events are below GBP 10m and there has been little change in the estimated net loss for each event during 2015.

Hurricane Odile struck the south-western coast of the US and Mexico in September. The losses from this event are below GBP 10m and there has been little change in the estimated net loss for each event during 2015.

named_events.loss_description: The current estimated ultimate claims for Tianjin are GBP 15.8m and GBP 14.8m gross and net of reinsurance. After allowing for inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums this reduces to GBP 13.5m.
The current estimated ultimate claims for the UK flood events are GBP 5.5m gross and GBP 4.5m net (also GBP 4.5m net of inwards and outwards reinstatement premiums).
Hurricane Patricia was the most notable of these, being the most powerful in the North-Eastern Pacific ever to make landfall. Patricia made landfall in a remotely populated area of Mexico.

named_events.event_name: PEMEX processing platform explosion and Chevron Bigfoot platform damage
named_events.loss_description: An explosion and fire at a PEMEX processing platform and severe tendon damage at Chevron's newly built 'Bigfoot' platform. Initial indications suggest very large losses (> $250m).
El Nio reduced hurricane activity in the North Atlantic, resulting insured losses were low; however El Nio also promoted development of intense tropical cyclones in the North-Eastern Pacific.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1084 opened 2015 with GBP 1,579.2m of gross claims outstanding. During 2015 the Syndicate recorded a prior-year release of GBP 95.7m (approximately 6.1% of opening gross reserves), driven predominantly by favourable claims development on attritional losses in the Energy, Casualty and Treaty divisions. The report highlights a number of named events in 2014 and 2015 (including Hurricane Odile, Hurricane Patricia, the Tianjin port explosion and UK floods); Tianjin and the UK floods had small estimated ultimate impacts to the Syndicate (GBP 15.8m gross / GBP 14.8m net for Tianjin; GBP 5.5m gross / GBP 4.5m net for UK floods).
